title: The Man of Steel Turns Disaster-Porn
review:
Clark Kent, Smallville, Krypton, Lex Luthor, Superman. These names ring a bell in a certain world of Superman. Once evolved cartoon series to movies. Now he is the man of steel.

This new Snyder-Nolan team up came with a totally different perspective and story line of the said Superman series. Say goodbye to Lana Lang as love interest and Lex Luthor as villain. In this movie, we've got the Clark Kent against people from his own planet, Krypton.

Though the movie was more of a disappointment, I highlighted some of the points I did not miss.

The story itself was fast-forwarded to answer the question, What becomes of Superman after Luthor and after Jonathan Kent?

Though it highlights several main points about the difficulty of discovering oneself, his love life, his struggles and his earthly- father's desire to keep his ability a secret, this movie has been more of Clark discovering Krypton.

When we say EPIC-FAIL, I think this was what the movie was all about. The presence of giant ships, and Jor-el's trench coat allows you to enter "The Matrix". Hey Keanu Reeves... Where Jor-El's presence is called "a shadow" from an "S"-shaped USB that the people from Krypton use also to maneuver the ship. Where the codex is not even an item that they are looking for but the codex it Clark Kent itself. Where the letter S is portrayed as a symbol for "hope". Where Lois Lane was asked by the aliens inside the ship for no reason at all. Where Martha Kent survived after being thrown by Zod and Zods men never did anything else than to disappear after he was taken by Superman in the city for more act of violence. Where New York was one block away from a farm without any sky-scrappers. Where Metropolis came into crumble but Superman never intended to help the people buried underneath the rubble. Where Zod was programmed to save Krypton even without the existence of Kryptonians. Where Lois Lane is an award winning Pulitzer journalist and I don't even have a clue why was that mentioned. Where moral-issue was highlighted but was unable to save his earthly father, standing helpless in front of a tornado. Where "you're not my real dad" script comes out of the context. Where Metropolis watch many people die when the man of steel was in nowhere but comes back in time to rescue Lois Lane. Where after snapping Zod's neck, Lois Lane appears for some reason. Where contrary to the Superman everyone knows of, this man of steel does not care about the people's safety and welfare. Where his weakness is not on Kryptonite but on killing (moral issue).

Though the movie was a THUMBS-DOWN on my viewpoint, I still highlighted some quotes from the movie that struck me. Just because you can't control me doesn't mean I'm your enemy. Faith comes first, trust will follow. You are my son. But somewhere out there you have another father, and he sent you here for a reason. And even if it takes you the rest of your life, you owe it to yourself to find out what that reason is. What if child dream of becoming something other than what society intended? What if a child aspire to something greater. Superman was once portrayed as a person from Krypton to save the people. In this movie, he was there to protect people. To save and protect are two different frames which were not highlighted in the movie. Maybe it was but it sucks.

The only part I love was how the two fathers, provided love, care and assistance to Clark.

review:

title: A great action filled Superhero movie
review:
Nothing more, nothing less.

Henry Cavill plays a great Superman, special FX were appealing to the eye, and enough action to keep me awake. A great start to a series of movies.

I look forward to part two, and I'm hoping for a little more character/relationship development among the characters, but other than that, complaining about this movie and how "unrealistic" it is sounds absurd. It's a Superhero movie - it's not real life!

My only complaint: why does the actress playing Lois Lane always made to look so mundane? Not only in this film, but Kate Bosworth in Superman Returns (2006) as well.

Sit back and enjoy. It really is a simple but attractive film filled with action and a great history recap about the story behind Superman.

title: Brlliant!
review: Finally, a director who gets 'adaptation'. Great costumes, superb casting, mesmerizing acting, edge of seat action sequences, convincing CGI, and award winning directing. And he did it all without a Lex Luther plot. Bravo! I'm looking forward to the Wonder Woman, and Justice League movies, and it would be a travesty not to keep Zack Snyder at the helm. Zack Snyder is a director who clearly understands superheroes and the fans who love them. I would really like to see Zack Snyder's, or even Joss Whedon's interpretation of X-Men. The existing directors and writers of the X-Men franchise have failed miserably.

title: Zoom Shot! Zoom Shot! ZOOOOOOOOM SHOT!!!!!!!!!!
review:
Something is flying *zoom shot*

Look at something fly over there *zoom shot*

There goes a spaceship for the nine thousandth time *zoom shot*

The amount of zoom shots in this movie actually summarize this movie fairly nicely and reveal a lot about this movie's faults. What is a zoom shot that is ever so slightly shaky used for? It is used for dramatic effect and it is used in small amounts so that when it is used it can make the scene much more dramatic. What does Man of Steel do?

EVERY SHOT MUST BE A ZOOM SHOT!!!

And there you have it. Man of Steel doesn't understand the timing and purpose of story elements. You like dramatic zoom shots? Have five hundred more! You like pretentious conversations? Have one every time someone opens their mouth. You like explosions? Come on over, we invited Michael Bay.

This movie tries too hard. It takes things that are good in small portions and throws them at you non-stop so that you are sick of them within the first twenty minutes of the movie. Never before have I seen so many conversations that try to have some deep and meaningful insight to mankind. The problem with this is that deep conversations don't pop out of nowhere. Usually meaningful conversations start off casual and then build into something more important. BUT THIS MOVIE DOESN'T BUILD UP TO ANYTHING! Want something meaningful? How about let's start the conversation with the meaning.

Imagine if you started a joke with the punchline... and then you started 50 other jokes with the punchline. Isn't the point of a joke the build- up to the punchline? That is another problem with Man of Steel. EVERYTHING HAPPENS SUDDENLY! There are no smooth transitions from one scene to the next.

While I will compliment the movie on some pretty nice action scenes, it still doesn't make it fantastic. It just simply makes it amusing and entertaining. I can't even say the acting is very good. The acting is okay, but it isn't top-notch by any means. Certain scenarios could've been easily avoided and didn't even make sense. Lois and Clark Kent kissing after possibly millions of people died? Who the heck would kiss IN THE ASHES OF A DESTROYED CITY?!?!? Lois Lane starts falling when next to a black hole... shouldn't she be sucked up in it like the rest of the buildings? People about to get lasered by Zod... let's not walk out of the way while Superman holds him down.

All in all, this movie is good for its explosions and the rare moments where it starts to look like an anime... those moments were pretty sweet.

title: Man of Steel - Disaster movie or superhero movie?
review:
When I think of Superman I think of what his father often said of him in all of the movies, "he will be revered as a God". Yet Superman just wanted to be human most of his childhood life. He never wanted to be special. So what happens when you are forced to go outside of yourself because you don't have a choice? Unfortunately you are not going to get any wisdom on that answer in this movie. I would say watch Superman 2. At least there Superman simply wanted Lois Lane. He wanted them to be together and to do that he sacrificed his powers to be with her. But then realized that who he is is more. The genius behind Superman 2 is he learned this through the green crystal which created his home and has been with him ever since. I believe this green crystal was what the Codex was in Man of Steel, but we never really are told what it is. It just seems to be the one piece of Krypton left that has a mysterious connection to Superman. In Man of Steel there is no mysterious connection, there is no fight to stay normal except of course during his adolescence and the only thing that helped him realize his full potential was a conversation he had with his real father who told him everything. So when his earth father told him he was an alien he wanted to be human but when his real alien father told he was an alien he accepted it. Okay.

Man of Steel is an over the top production of building exploding, CGI speed-up and CGI everything else. 95% of this movie appears to be shot in front of a green screen and the effects for the people look just as bad as they do in The Matrix Reloaded. The fact these aliens can move super fast was a great reveal at first but when it happened throughout the movie it got boring fast. The problem is we see special effects like this all the time now. Special effects for the most part are not a movie. If you base your whole movie on them the movie will suffer. This is exactly the issue with Man of Steel and since the sequel is already in the works we can expect none of these issues to be resolved.

Henry Cavill is not interesting as Superman, in fact he looks outright bored in this movie. Michael Shannon actually steals most of this movie and although his character is the most built of any character in the movie, he is still overshadowed by all the effects surrounding him. Does Zach believe that effects are more important than characters and acting? I guess so.

As a special effect extravaganza this movie has it all. As a movie with a plot, interesting characters, good acting, enjoyable movie, this movie has none of that. I was interested in what was going on maybe twice. But the minute we see Superman take zero care of human life by crashing into everything purposely during a fight after we were told for over an hour he doesn't want to lose his temper and hurt anyone or kill anyone and that he his moral, the entire movie itself takes a tailspin. Therefore Superman is a hypocrite. Also Zod as a religious fanatic was a great idea but unfortunately religious fanatics don't work the way he does. By the climax he goes from being a fanatic to being a mad scientist. Certainly some fanatics have committed genocide but we were never led to understand why in Zod's case. He just decided it was for the best.

Awful movie. Just watch Christopher Reeve in Superman 1 and 2. Those movies get Superman. They nail the comic book more than anything else that has come after it.

title: A misunderstanding
review: Directed by 47-yeard-old Zack Snyder, Man of Steel is like a 10-year-olds visualization of what a superhero movie would be. It's loud, show-off-y, and packed with special effects; it also lacks sense, story, or anything engaging for more than two minutes. Where the plot isn't flat and paper thin, it's ridiculously predictable; where it isn't predictable - it just doesn't make any sense because of the various inconsistencies (example: the first time the aliens are landing on Earth, TV stations are broadcasting this news along with "amateur footage", featuring a major close-up of the ship. Yet when Clark goes out to see it, you can see the ship is very far away, only visible to human eye as nothing more than a slightly bigger shooting star. Only using his supervision is he able to get the magnification... shown a minute ago on the TV screen). As far as acting goes, Adams', Cavill's and Lane's performances are up to part, but even they cannot save the movie from destruction. But it's the story (or the lack of one) is Man of Steel's biggest issue - it feels rushed, carelessly fabricated on your way to work. If you top it off with annoying product placement (thank you, Nokia and Nikon, I'll stay away from your products) - you have a complete and utter disaster on your hands; one that, I feel, not even the Superman could salvage the Earth from.

title: Mediocre and Disjointed Effort
review:
The latest attempt at making a movie about the legendary Superman has followed the ill fates of all the movies before it. Much like the Christopher Nolan Batman movies, "Man of Steel" reboots the story line to tell us the origin of the hero. However, where "Batman Begins" did this successfully, "Man of Steel" fails in its entirety.

The biggest issue I had with "Man of Steel" is how disjointed the movie was. It begins on Krypton when Kal El is sent to Earth after the failed coup of General Zod. After this prologue, we are immediately taken to see Clark working on an Oil Rig and saving the lives of man other men. As Clark makes his way through life, the viewer is treated (so to speak) to various non sequential flashbacks about his childhood. Rather than follow a linear pattern which is introduced in the film, the modern events continuously and sloppily jump back and forth in the past and present, resulting in a nonsensical mess.

One of the worst things about the movie is the death of Jonathan Kent. It is so melodramatic as the man simply stands there and lets a tornado slowly take him for apparently no real reason. It is supposed to be Kent's wish to save his son's abilities from exposure, but it is a futile attempt. With as quick as Clark can move, he could not only have saved his dad, but with the ample time given by the slow moving tornado, it appears Jonathan could have simply walked away from it. In the end, we end up with an attempt to mimic the scene in "Spider-Man" where the dying father figure passes an important life lesson to his son. However, no real lesson can be derived.

The fight scenes are not even good enough to save this dull movie. They are hard to follow, with the adversaries moving so fast that all the viewers see are flashes of fighting with colors indicating where each character is. They have some good moments but are mostly mediocre and boring.

A oft mentioned criticism of this film is that Superman kills Zod at the end of the film, against the well established moral compass of Superman. This, however, did not bother me at all. Superman was put in a position where he could allow a man to willingly and purposely murder innocent people and the only option he had was to kill the would be murderer. He made the only choice available to him.

While this was not the worst comic book movie ever made, it definitely ranks up high with them. When it was over, I felt nothing for any of the characters other than embarrassment that the writers would saddle them with such a lousy ending. It was painful.

I cannot really recommend this movie, but I cannot dismiss it either. Different people with different likes will have different impressions of it. For me, however, this film was dreadful and I will never rewatch it. A poor, poor effort.

title: Not good/ not terrible
review:
First of all I am no superhero movie fan, I read some comics when I was a kid of course but never delved into the universe as much as some here have done. So I don't have any quarrels with changes as long as we get a great performance and a nicely fitting story. I would also like to point out I watch movies for the story not for cheap thrills, so movies like Transformers/Expendables/John Carter and more of those mindless drones are not for me.

The editing is pretty bad and I would even go so far by saying that it broke the movie for instance they show Clark wearing a cape witnessed by his dad at the end of the movie, they should have done it in the beginning to show that father Kent saw his foster sons potential. The jumping back and forth between then and now using the latest flashback technology from Krypton breaks consistency as well. If they have shown a linear growing up movie, they might even incorporate the fact that it takes time to get really powerful or have taken time to explain that Superman is also different(stronger ) on a genetic level so it can be made believable that one farm boy can beat a squadron of equally powerful individuals who were trained as soldiers. Instead they cram in as much (raw)material as they can, throw it in a blender take of the lid and let it splash the kitchen hoping that no one sees what they threw into the blender but show people how clean the kitchen is when they were done cleaning up.

There is no real story/plot discernible in the entire movie. I wasn't expecting Tolkien, Dickens or Tolstoy but from Nolan/Goyer I expected a bit more depth in the characters and story. The dark knight would be a great thriller if you would take the Batman element out of it. If you take the Superman element out of this movie there is no movie left, the closest it would come to is an independence day like movie. Also the Terraforming bit is ridiculous, if Kryptonians would have developed their technology to this level, why not pick Mars? Ask Superman for some blood so they can rebuild their home on Mars and done! For an advanced society, like that on Krypton apparently, I find it strange that no one except Superman could escape. I could have believed it if it was a sudden thing without warning whatsoever and that Superman was send out by his parents because of a genocide type situation or maybe a strange custom where kryptonians send out their newborn to experience other civilizations( DBZ anyone? ;) ), but no they even had time for a full criminal trial. IF Jor El was correct they even had a couple of weeks so they could save several thousands Also using the codex as a plot device is very poor since it doesn't really relate at a human level( it doesn't play into emotion-Pathos-), what they should have done is create a storyline where it actual makes sense to people why Zod goes to earth and wants to kill superman, just a small example: Supermans mother was bethrotted to Zod because it had the perfect genetic match( or maybe even something more traditional or earth like as a caste system), but instead she falls in love with Jor El, gets pregnant of him. Zod finds out and wants to kill Jor El and his son at which point Jor El who already had taken precautions shoots his son towards earth in a newly designed ship. Since there is no proof of a son Zod get's sentenced to the phantom zone for 20 years for assault, Jor El marries Supermans mother and thus creating the final hate that will consume Zod in hunting down Superman.

The only reason that this movie is even remotely watchable is because the actors themselves carry their respective roles and try to make the best of it, the VFX made the turd slightly better watchable as well but if you are not carried away by the hype it can only take you so far.

This is at best a mediocre movie, it had great potential but fell short in a lot of ways...

title: Amazed but not what I expected
review:
I always view films for the first time with no expectations and no preconceptions about what the movie should be like. This is exactly what you need to do for this film, if you are expecting it to be like any other superman you've ever seen you will be disappointed.

The movie has more of a sci-fi feel than a superhero fell but thats exactly what it is, Superman is an alien after all.

Action scenes in this film blow any other out the water in terms of scale of destruction.

Cavill plays superman well and will look forward to seeing how he plays Clark Kent in the sequel.

title: Superman A Must Watch
review:
A problem a necessity leads to a solution or a re-invention. But what if a super human personality searches for answers? What if the choices for him were made and still he has to make a choice? Man of Steel is not just about the cape wearing super hero who can bite a bullet and x ray you. It's not about the super powers he has and how he uses them. It's about how a father defies the world he knows for giving his son the ability to choose. How Jor El even after his death provides an avenue to his Son Kal El to discover himself. How Jonathan Kent helps Clark Kent harness and control his powers and maintain a low profile in this world where his super powers may be perceived as alien and lead to his alienation. Man of steel is about Clark Kent's search for who he is? Where he comes from and how he has these incredible powers. It's about how Lois Lane picks up trails and tracks of Greenhorn a shrimp fisherman who mysteriously disappears after an accident on an oil rig, a bar tender who leaves the bar after being provoked by a drunk brawler but does not budge. How she discovers who this supernatural being is who seems to come out of nowhere to help people and silently disappears. As a story Arc Man of Steel has a villain who is equal to Super Man and wreaks havoc on earth searching for him as Super Man is the last son of Krypton and holds the key to the dead planets emergence again. General Zod searches out planets and arrives at earth understanding the key to his quest is on earth. He holds the earth at ransom and out comes Kal El/Clark Kent but now fondly called Superman by the people. Superman takes on General Zod in an epic battle which pits General Zod as an equal adversary whom Superman has to finally kill in battle. The story unfolds much better on screen with the effects and epic battles. But one question to all those whiners who complain about Superman killing General Zod?

Why not look at this point in Superman's journey as the pivotal point where he decides as a principle not to kill anyone? For more on the action sequences they are better watched on screen. Henry Cavill looks every bit the Super character he is and also has that adoring and lovable smile which makes him the innocent looking Clark Kent. The photography is awesome in the movie and there are a few easter eggs to all DC Comic fans where Lex Luthor is referred and also Bruce Wayne(Batman's) Wayne Enterprises is mentioned.

title: A thrilling and breathtaking plunge into the Superman mythos!
review:
After reading critics reviews and witnessing first hand the hostility that Superman fans have toward this movie on the message boards, I was expecting this film to be truly terrible. A mere ho-hum film that would scant be worth my $9.00 admission (well $18, my girlfriend came too) I was pleasantly surprised to see that reviewers were giving it much too hard of a time, because it was fantastic!

I never say this about a movie, but I was literally gobsmacked. After watching this film, I can't help but concede this small fact: the movie garnered so much hate from critics because Zack Snyder rubs them the wrong way. He makes movies that HE wants to see, he makes them from the perspective of the fan and what THEY want to watch up on the big screen. I mean, I can't say I blame them for disliking Snyder, since he doesn't have much quality to his name, but it can't be denied that he really did Superman justice with this film. What quality his name has really shows in this film. The execution was exactly what Superman needed; because what is Superman if not a world filled with action, lives to be saved, and tough decisions to be made.

And for those who say that it was out of character for Kal El to kill Zod? He needed to kill Zod. Why you ask? That's simple. It's because Zod was blood thirsty; he wouldn't stop terrorizing Earth until he died, he said so himself before he and Kal took their fight to the skies. "This will end one of two ways Kal, either you die, or I do." Zod would have incinerated that innocent family had Kal not stopped him by killing him. There was no other way to stop Zod, because now that he was gaining power from the yellow sun, he was just as strong as Kal, perhaps even stronger, since he was born and bred to be a warrior. Zod's suit served to hone his strength, and when he shed the suit, he was better for it, having years of experience fighting on Kal, with all his training with that immense weight of the suit on his shoulders. Kal's choice was simple: let Zod kill that family and stand idly by, like he did when he let his father die, or step in and do something drastic. Also, this was his first romp as Superman: Zod was a maniac who couldn't be stopped, he was a murderer, a tyrant, and a lunatic. He murdered Jor-El in cold blood, and admitted that he would gladly do it again. He wanted to exact mass genocide on Earth and almost succeeded. Is that not enough to kill him? If you recall, Bruce Wayne let Ra's Al Ghul die for MUCH less than that, and no one batted an eye at that. You can say that Bruce let Ra's die and didn't physically kill him, but the whole scene with the train and the blowing up of the tracks was all his doing. He orchestrated the entire situation, and then let Ra's die rather than save him. Kal did what he needed to do, and killing Zod didn't make me hate him. As a matter of fact, it made me pity him, it made me feel how human he is, it made me like him for his faults and for his portrayal as a broken individual, rather than for being the epitome of perfection. For his entire life, Clark was forced by his parents to keep himself a secret; Jonathan and Martha damaged him psychologically, and all at once, he was forced to abandon a lifetime of repression and embrace who he was and show the world. He was thrust into being a hero without having time to prepare for it. And I think he did a damn good job with what he had.

Man of Steel was a thrill ride, and it was simply a great superhero film. If we could go in with open minds and not critics' expectations, we would enjoy films a whole lot more. Now, that's not to say that if you share a critic's opinion that you're wrong. That's not what I'm saying; after all, you're entitled to your opinion. I'm merely saying that personally, I really enjoyed this film. Snyder did a miraculous job modernizing Superman and making him relatable to us as a whole. I mean, xenophobia is a current and pressing issue, so why not explore it in the easiest way possible?

Plus, and let's be frank and not kid ourselves here, if Snyder and Nolan's names were switched on the marquee, this movie would have had MUCH more critical acclaim than it presently has now.

9/10 for me. It's as simple as that!

title: Superman returns... a lot better this time.
review:
It's been seven years since the last time we saw Superman on the big screen in Superman Returns, which didn't even have too bad of reviews. But as years went on, the hate began. I didn't think it was that bad, though it was way too long, Brandon Routh was sort of dull, and I myself have just never really been big on the character.

Now he's back in Man of Steel. And he's gotten a makeover. Metropolis, Superman's city, is glum. Why? Because Christopher Nolan, easily the finest filmmaker in the business, co-wrote the script with David S. Goyer. Both of them penned The Dark Knight Trilogy, arguably one of the finest trilogies of them all. In the director's chair is Zack Snyder, a director I've never been too fond of.

Now, the question is, is it any good? Does it live up to it's cast and crew? I'm not sure if I'm quite the right person to ask, considering all I know about Superman are the basic things (his name, kryptonite, Lois Lane, Lex Luthor, Metropolis, works as a journalist). I'm just not that crazy about Superman. Typically, if Christopher Nolan has a movie coming out, I have a seizure due to excitement (joking obviously). But since he's not directing it but is still involved, I felt it wouldn't hurt to try it. Now, some people hate this movie, and others don't exactly love it. So, it's my turn.

Let's begin with the plot. Consider this movie "Superman: The Beginning." It shows how Kal-El a.k.a. Clark Kent a.k.a. Superman (Henry Cavill, looking confident in the role) came to Earth from Krypton, grew up with Ma and Pa Kent (Diane Lane and Kevin Costner, who are just too right for this movie), and was forced to live a low profile. You know, cause he's Superman. A half hour into the movie, we meet journalist Lois Lane (Amy Adams, who better?), who is rescued by Superman and is quickly fascinated. But Clark's quiet life is about to come to a halt. General Zod (Michael Shannon, who is just too good at being bad), has a vendetta out for Superman, and plans on bringing Krypton to Earth. But there isn't enough room for Kryptonians and humans too.

I think what works about Man of Steel is just how deep the writers dig into Superman. Also, the mood of it is also right. Everyone here is well casted. Yes, they did a bit of tampering with the story line (out with the kryptonite and the fact that Clark's a journalist), but they did it with good reason. Also, the movie is a tad too long and some of the action sequences, though spectacular, drag on.

But everyone here seems to be having a good time and everyone is good at what they do, so let them do it. Is it on par with The Dark Knight Trilogy? Uh, no. Snyder and Nolan are two very different people. Man of Steel isn't the best movie of the summer, but it is a good one. I'm sure many will disagree with me, and let them. I don't care. I thought it was really good. Iron Man 3 is better, but this is still the Superman movie we've been waiting for.

B+

title: An enjoyable summer blockbuster.
review:
When I heard that Zack Snyder was going to be directing the next Superman movie, with Christopher Nolan as a producer, I was reasonably excited. I was expecting an instant classic. What I got did not disappoint, but this movie did need work.

To start off with, the script probably needed to be looked over again. There seemed to be a few superfluous characters, like Lois Lane. She really did not need to be in this movie. There could have just been a little nod to her character (like the appearance of the LexCorp logo), which would have been a good basis for future sequels. I enjoyed Amy Adams' performance, but she could have been written out almost entirely.

The action was well done, but it was a bit shaky at times. Combine that with the 3D and the IMAX screen I was watching it on, and it does become a bit overwhelming. I probably won't have this problem when it's released on DVD/Blu-Ray, but it seems as though the filmmakers were really banking on the audience seeing it in either 3D or IMAX (or both).

What I did enjoy were Michael Shannon, Russell Crowe and Kevin Costner. All three of these men stole the show and made "Man of Steel" worth the price of admission. The cinematography was beautiful and the music by Hans Zimmer was spectacular. The special effects were well done and there definitely was a good amount of character development with this young Superman. The film also left enough room for the character to grow with possible future installments.

title: Overall an awesome movie to watch with minor complaints
review:
So, being a life long Superman fan loving the Christopher Reeve movies (even though 1 and 2 came out 4 years before I was born), this movie was really the movie I have always wanted to see. I have always wanted to see what Superman could truly do if put into a situation where he had no choice but to unleash his powers in entirety.

What's GREAT about this movie IMO. The special affects are top notch and made me feel like what I was watching could actually happen one day. The powers on display were truly alien and AWESOME. Henry Cavill portrays a brooding, emotionally fragile, serious, and complex Man of Steel. The critics have all of those characteristics CORRECT. But in my opinions that what Superman should be. He has great powers and abilities and we all know that comes with serious responsibility. We see a struggling man in this movie because he is a young Superman and is unsure of himself or his powers...Can't ALL of us relate to that? If you can't relate to that then you are not human. So, Henry Cavill is GREAT.I also loved Faora's character. Evil, moraless, powerful, and confident...She was great. Lastly, I really feel like the way Zod went out was perfect. There was NO other choice for Superman given the situation. I think maybe they could have showed him try to move Zod off that spot and be unsuccessful to create the illusion of really having no choice but I think that part was just a given. What do Police officer's do in that situation? They made me relate to it that way and I commend them for it. No jail holds Zod and no other way has been established yet to nullify a Kryptonians powers so the fight would have continued and more people may have died...No need for that and Superman did what he had to and killed Zod. Period. End of Debate.

#1. The way Kal-El gets the suit. So there is this scout ship that landed on Earth 20,000 years ago and it happens to contain a house of EL Kyrptonian suit? Common Goyer get your poop together on this one. I am all about stretching the mythology to fit a plot in a movie but this whole education scene was too rushed for me and not mythical or epic at all...To me it would have made much much more sense to create some suspense to this scene and also have the suit sent to Earth with baby Kal in his ship...Maybe, they could have wrote it so once the S key was entered into the scout ship it activated baby Kal's ship and had it automatically sent to where the scout ship was and have it land inside and have the suit float out of the ship...Much more dramatic, practical, and exciting IMO. Goyer dropped the mythology ball with this one. The SUIT is IMPORTANT.

#2 If Kyrpton was going to explode in a couple days, why imprison Zod and his gang in the phantom zone? Wouldn't it be more practical to just let them suffer Krypton's fate like the rest of them? To me, it would have made 1000% more sense to have Zod and his gang figure out a way to flee krypton on their own by stealing some ships.

#3 Again, with the phantom Zone thing. Why exactly was it just the Kryptonian's and their ships that get pulled into the phantom zone black hole...A freaking black whole would suck the entire population of metropolis into it..Bad writing. Should have happened in space to make it more believable. I also don't like that they had to put 2 phantom drives against each other to open the black hole...No intelligence with that one. To me, Faora could have stopped that entire sequence on her own using her abilities. Should have made Superman come up with a trick or Dr. Hamilton come up with a trick...

#4 I think the destruction of the cities of smallville and metropolis are fine but I think the way they handled the alien invasion should have shocked people and should have been portrayed with people starting to evacuate the major cities around the world when the ships started showing up...This would have cut out all the crap people are talking about Superman not caring about innocents when this destruction is going on...They should have implied that most people were gone and the city was empty. I am not sure really if they were or not and that's why it doesn't make sense...Goyer should have showed people leaving so this debate wouldn't happen.

#5 My BIGGEST issue with this movie is the death of Johnathan Kent. After seeing it twice the whole death scene is STUPID. Completely, utterly stupid writing by Goyer. Dude, Superman can move faster than people can see and he could have saved his Dad with no one seeing it. I had no problem with the scene playing out up until he gets hit by the tornado. To make it more interesting and to show Clark that he is not God and he can't save everyone they should have done it like this. OK, keep everything that happened up until Johnathan goes to get the dog. Have him run back to the car, free the dog and in the meantime show him sweating and struggling. Have him come out of the car and collapse of a heart attack...Have Clark rush over to realize that his Dad is dead and died not from the tornado but from a heart attack.

I had a lot more written but had to cut it out. Again great movie with minor complaints and I look forward tot he sequels!

title: First gay Superman
review:
As some critics have already noticed, the latest Superman-franchise has more Christian parables than any of them before. But it's also the most obvious gay-adaptation of the myth, and in a very good way.

The Nolan&Snyder-version is the first movie version of Superman that emphasizes the character is super_sensitive_. The supernatural _powers_ are in minimal use before the final half an hour of the movie, and you can easily see that the "last battle" is so long (as a matter of routine) just to fulfill the expectations of the superhero genre -audience. If you cut out the first and last 30 minutes of the film, you'd get quite super Superman-movie.

The latest Superman is hardly first one with dazzlingly beautiful face, but this time we see him also in many other "role clothes" than his blueboy uniform, accentuating both the old fashion masculinity _and_ the gender role play. This Superman is actually the first one whose story is a strong "coming out" -story and whose secret is a "beautiful truth", as his mother confesses in the last part of the film.

This subtle way of adaptation is the reason why I liked especially the pasolinian moments (levitation scene from "Teorema", desert-scene from "The Gospel..") that director Snyder has used to stress what kind of messiah we have this time, and also the reconciliation between gay hero and US army.

title: Started epically, but took a wrong turn!!
review:
In the first hour of the movie I was pretty much excited, touched by the performances and grabbed to my seat, but by the end it disappointed me. Anyway, I gotta say that there are more good sides to this movie than bad, so lets start with the bad and save the good stuff in the end.

What disappointed me: Despite being the hottest superman ever, and doing a superb job physically, still Henry Cavill's acting could have been better. If the movie intends to make the story of Superman more humane and realistic, then Henry should have given a much deeper and/or natural performance, instead he was a bit numb at times. Second, the dialog turned very cheesy in the middle of the film, it just disconnected me from the movie and turned the most dramatic lines into comedy. Third, the action scenes were too much, I know its a Chris Nolan thing, but it was hard to keep track of the story from the numerous explosions that just prolonged the movie, at some point I didn't understand what was going on.

What impressed me: The portrayal of the world of Cripton, it was very well put together (the characters, the technology, the costumes, the planet) it really does justice to the background story of Cripton and to the origins of Superman. Second, the Acting. Kevin Costner and Diane Lane give such heart-felt performances, they really give depth to the Kent family and the role they had in raising Clark/Cal. Similarly Russel Crowe and Ayelet Zurer as his real parents delivered very good performances as well. What was more impressive is the redefinition of Superman as a hero: This movie really rebuilds the character of Cal and makes him more human, instead of hiding his humanity behind the stereotypical image of Superman. The fact that not everyone was routing for Superman, waiting for him to bring them salvation and heavily labeling him as a hero throughout the whole movie. The word 'Superman' actually was only said once or twice in the whole movie. Apart from all this, the special effects were indeed out of this world!!! They were rendered magnificently by true visual effects artists who are the real heroes behind this movie. It just shows the amount of effort put in the film. Another thing that I loved is the fact that Louis knows the identity of Superman. Finally a superman movie where Louis is not such a fool and knows that Clark Kent is Superman. Its a hole that was finally filled in this movie.

Well that's it basically. Like I said the good side outnumber the bad, but the bad side has a very influential role on the perception of the film, its what sadly made me leave the theater with remaining feelings of distress from the extensive action scenes and disappointment from the story, when I ought to have been amazed and excited for future sequels.

title: You Will Believe
review:
Superman is Jesus. This thematic subtext is hardly new. But Superman as a Jesus who only reluctantly accepts his mantle of saviour of humankind, and inwardly harbours a childish bitterness and resentment? A Superman who maliciously enjoys the secret thrill of being able to let loose and finally hit back, channeling decades of repression and bullying trauma into a succession of world-shattering punches, released with gleeful abandon? Much more Scorsese Jesus than Jesus Christ Superstar. This, as the inevitable comparison has it, is a far cry from the venerated days of Christopher Reeve.

To say this is a Superman who speaks to this day and age would be retreading a cliché already ground into redundancy from overuse. The temptation to run rampant with clichés such as "More 'Superman Begins' than 'Superman Returns'" is overwhelming. And, yet, such clichés are the stock that heroes are born of, and continually validated by. Zack Snyder and David S. Goyer are both certainly fearless in tapping into the essence and mythos of the character, navigating clichés of classicism and 'dark and gritty reboot' ethos with grace and tact. Indeed, to say this the first Superman film that fully, satisfyingly, explores not only the cultural function of Superman but plumbs the depths of Kal-El/Clark Kent himself would not be an overstatement.

Man of Steel is, if nothing else, overwhelming. The film is a relentless sensory overload, a breathless symphony of dazzling special effects, staggering scope of destruction (The Avengers now takes second place in collateral construction damage), and brutal, kinetic and frequently airborne fight choreography. From the first minutes, boldly opening with Russell Crowe's Jor-El riding a space dragon amidst the explosions of the dying planet Krypton undergoing a military coup. Already, Man of Steel has delivered one of the best (albeit microcosmic) sci-fi films in years. And, by this point, there is more than another two hours to go.

It scarcely slows down, only hitting the pause button to allow dual dads Crowe and Kevin Costner (both as good at frowning and grunting as ever) to deliver stern monologues ratcheting Kal/Clark between divine purpose and personal choice. It also scarcely quiets down, as Hans Zimmer's magnificent score continuously bludgeons the audience with horns, drums and strings enough to leave the most desensitized audience member gasping for breath. Stunning is the word at hand, as seldom before has watching a movie felt so much like a workout. This is far from a bad thing, but hardly a relaxing watch.

Nor, as most reviews have taken great pains to express, is levity on the table. Gone is the frivolity of Gene Hackman's prancing Lex Luthor and the bumbling slapstick of Reeve's Kent. This is a Superman prone to gritting his teeth rather than flashing toothy grins. Again, this is not a bad thing. The 'Nolan influence' is overwhelming, as the film even echoes the non- linear flashback structure of his seminal Batman Begins. Equally, intentionally or not, the film alludes to countless offerings from rival company Marvel, from the 'enhanced senses overload' purloined from Daredevil to the palpable glee of experimenting with powers of Spider-Man to military banter reminiscent of Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer to flying shots lifted directly from Iron Man.

However, Man of Steel is far from a derivative mess. In lieu of jokiness is enough sentiment to flood Metropolis. Melodrama too, granted. It is interesting to notice the film's unabashed embracing of the character being appropriated as an American cultural icon (one jaw- dropping Freudian slip minimizes Superman 'acting in the world's interests' into 'acting in America's interests'). But it is hard not to be pounded into willful submission by the film's incessant pace and noise into full embracing of the deluge of big, loud sentiment and purpose. Man of Steel hits hard, but hits undeniably true.

It will be quiet the challenge to un-see Henry Cavill as Superman, as with past examples of the role resulting in extreme-typecasting-turned-career-stunting (poor Brandon Routh). However, Cavill's sublime embodiment of one of the trickiest characters to sell demonstrates an actor of extreme talent rather than limited range. As much as Cavill owns every angsty grimace and serene smile, it is the gleeful abandon he shows when 'letting loose', whether flying around the planet at top speed or bludgeoning Kryptonian adversaries, that truly calcifies his humanity. Amy Adams does her considerable best with feisty reporter Lois Lane, but is still limited by underwritten characterization that leaves her inclusion often feeling like an afterthought. There is no doubt, too, that audiences will take some acclimatizing to Michael Shannon's screaming, spit-spewing performance (his "I WILL FIND HIM!" scene, while fated to become almost as meme-worthy as Terrence Stamp's "Kneel", is still a bit much), yet there is no doubt his unflinchingly resolute Zod is entirely right for the film, and a more than worthy adversary. Diane Lane's quiet performance, conversely, is a tremendous asset, providing much needed warmth and whimsy to the film as Clark's beloved 'Ma'.

Man of Steel is not a perfect film. The pacing and exposition often stumble over themselves (how exactly does Crowe's space-ghost work exactly? Never mind), and, ironically, the moments of attempted, shoehorned-in humour are often the film's weakest (Lois' thoughts on first kisses proves an unintentionally comic non-sequitar). But, as Snyder and Goyer are careful to stress, Superman is not perfect either. And, like Superman, it is easy to get swept up in the overwhelming desire to invest in the iconicity of a hero, and forgive the inevitable shortcomings. You will believe a man can fly. You will believe a hero capable of unspeakable violence. And you will believe in him, and his movie, nonetheless.

-9/10

title: A must watch for Superman fans !!!
review:
The movie boasts of an amazing team put together by Christopher Nolan and Zack Snyder along with wonderful star cast of Russel Crowe , Diane lane and Laurence Fishburne.

Man of Steel focuses on the evolution of Superman who is forced to confront his secret when the Earth is invaded by his distant relatives. He must fight back in order to save earth from falling into pit.

From the director of 300 , Watchmen and The Legend of the Guardian , Zack Synder gives you a visual delight which is full of unbelievable and amazing actions sequences. Clearly, this is the best Superman movie in terms of special effects where Zack Snyder lives up to his reputation for creating visually stunning movies. The film has a very good storyline as it portrays the emotional struggle of Superman as he tries to control his powers and is very enthusiastic about using them for good.. What lets the film down is the narrative as too little time is devoted to the evolution of Superman. His transition to Superman under his Krypton father's guidance is shown very weakly and not enough time is dedicated to show the relationship between Superman and his Earth father as this relationship is one of the key factors which makes Superman who he is. Not much time is dedicated to highlight the plight of Superman as he feels more alien when he discovers his power. Instead the movie turns out to be a slug fest exploiting technological advancements in CGI. There is a double climax in the movie which proves to be visually destructive and violent which makes you feel that such large scale destruction was a bit too much. Nevertheless, there is a substance behind the destructive climax as two equally powerful superheroes collide but this may be a bit too much for audience to digest. Kevin Costner who plays the Earth father of Superman impresses in the few moments he has on screen. Henry Cavill, did a commendable job as Superman, but had was very little emotion on his face. Happiness, sadness, anger, love were all the same. Other actors did justice to their part.

For people expecting something like Batman Begins as this comes from Nolan's production house, this movie may let them down. A must watch for Superman fans but the movie may not make a lot of new fans for this ageless superhero. If a next movie is being planned, we would suggest that a great villain be selected and focus be paid a little more to the emotional aspects of Superman and why he is the great character that he is, thanks to the upbringing of his Earth parents.

Good - 3.5/5

title: Love it or Hate it
review:
There seem to have two parts in this movie: cinematography side and story telling side since two strong players are in the making of this movie.

It's just another Snyder movie with Nolan's spice on it. You either love it or hate it.

I like 300 and Sucker Punch but I dislike Watchmen (story telling part). As for Man of Steel, I like it because it is a Watchmen style with Sucker Punch touch. The action is great as a comical character has to be superb. Snyder succeeded to make the man of steel really powerful visually. Compared to previous attempt to make this comical character come to life, Snyder has pushed the benchmark a lot higher.

That's the artistic side.

As for the story telling part, if you like Nolan's approach to reboot a superhero instalment such as Batman Begins and so forth, you'll love Man of Steel. He is very good at making a comic believable in our current worldly sense. Nolan can really make the superheroes come to life. He is able to make anything logical and believable although they are just a character in a comic.

I think the directors are smart enough to choose Snyder to take care of cinematography side and Nolan to tell the story with Zimmer to create the atmosphere. They work pretty well when they are mixed together.

Some may not like it as the story and the visual effects are somewhat disconnected. Especially the romance part, it is still not there. But I anticipate the romance to grow substantially in the coming instalments. To explain the origin of a man who can fly is already exhaustive. Nevertheless, the emotion between Superman and his natural parents and guardians is exceptional. But the restraint of Superman to use his power before wearing the superman suit feels a bit constipated. This is the only downside of this movie.

Just treat it as Superman Begins, you'll love it as it explains completely the origin of Superman (although it may sway a bit away from the original comics but it is OK as long as it makes sense). If you expect a Reeve's type of Superman, you won't.

title: This movie reached my expectations in an exceeding manner!
review:
I remember seeing the teaser and being utterly stung with curiosity and excitement. As a relatively sizeable Superman fan, my expectations were not of different caliber. On the contrary, they were very high and I must say, this product of brilliance did not disappoint regardless of the few plot holes I couldn't help but noticing. For the people that are complaining about its alleged lack of emotions and abridgement of a good romantic element, I strongly beg to differ. I believe Zack Snyder did an excellent job in conveying the sheer despair felt by Clark Kent being conflicted with the brink of humanity's likely extinction as he ventured into what he had been profusely in disaccord with all throughout his life; his destiny. Furthermore, the genuine empathetic emotions are not just limited to the protagonist, far from it, we also receive a quite marvelous performance by Laurence Fishburne. At various moments in the movie, he illustrates his wisdom in a unique way and delivers to us his angst such as the moment he held the hand of Jenny convinced that it was the end.

Moreover, not only was I impressed with the acting, but I was also blown away by the visuals and art work of this film. The CGI was to say the least breathtaking. The longing impact of a Kriptonian's fist on one of its companions was immensely stimulating. The loud sound effects gave birth to wonders for us spectators in terms of truly feeling the strength and brutality of their inconceivable might. As for the music, you can clearly witness Hans Zimmer's genius in the meticulousness and applicability of each song composed; thoroughly spectacular.

In conclusion, though the plot might not be the most sophisticated achievement in cinema, this movie is certainly worth the time and cost. I was earnestly invested in its exquisite visuals, mind-boggling brawls, rather compelling character development, and beautifully composed music from the very beginning to the conclusion of "Man of Steel". I recommend this movie to everyone, regardless of whether you are into comics or not. The overall experience of this movie surpasses whatever meager flaws and defects it abides.

title: You're the Answer, Son
review:
Greetings again from the darkness. 75 years ago, the first Superman comic book was published. It would be quite challenging to name very many kids who have not imagined themselves as Superman at some point during that time. Numerous Superman re-boots have occurred in various media: comics, TV, movies, video games, toys, etc., and the bigger the fan, the more etched in mind what the Man of Steel should look and act like. Woe to the filmmaker who doesn't share that fan's vision.

Enter director Zack Snyder, writer David S Goyer, and writer/producer Christopher Nolan. This triumvirate has been responsible for such comic based movie material as The Dark Knight franchise, 300, Watchmen, and Blade. Some of the criticisms of this most recent Superman presentation include a lack of fun, the absence of humor, no love story, too much backstory, an overabundance of action and CGI, and a hero that is much too serious ... and that's a list ignoring the outcry over the redesigned suit sans red briefs. As with anything, the closer to the heart, the less amenable to change folks become. At least no one is complaining about the lack of phone booths!

This movie has quite the balance of visual effects and backstory. It's clearly designed to be the first in a series, and because of that, we get the foundation of Superman: the rare natural born baby on the planet Krypton - a planet speeding towards destruction. Jor-El (Russell Crowe) executes his plan to save his newborn son Kal-El by rocketing him off to Earth. While that's happening, General Zod (Michael Shannon) stages one of the most ill-timed coups ever ... he tries to seize control of the dying planet. This opening sequence is filled with some of the biggest, loudest effects of the whole movie. It's a jolting start that I wasn't particularly fond of, but it's obviously well done and with purpose.

Kal-El lands on earth and becomes known as Clark Kent, adopted son of Kansas farmers played by Diane Lane and Kevin Costner. Most of Clark's childhood is glimpsed through flashbacks of specific events, and serves the purpose of giving us a taste, while not delaying the appearance of Superman ... though that name is only heard once (maybe twice). In an attempt to hide his powers, Clark becomes a drifter. However, it's impossible to keep your superhero powers secret when you rescue a group of oil rig workers by using your super strength.

Enter Daily Planet super-reporter Lois Lane (Amy Adams). She's good at her job and easily figures out the big secret. But rather than contact TMZ for a giant pay day, Lois understands that this may be something the world just isn't ready to hear. Wise lady. The relationship between Lois and Clark is rudely interrupted by the reappearance of General Zod and his right hand lady-warrior (Antje Traue). See, Zod thinks he can takeover Earth and re-establish his Krypton roots ... and Superman holds the key to his plan.

If you are a Superman fan, all of this makes perfect sense. If not, I suspect this movie will not hold much interest for you. If you are a fan of the 1978 version with Christopher Reeve, I would encourage you to keep an open mind. While that version wallowed in frivolous whimsy, this one is a bit darker and more philosophical ... what you might expect from an alien with super powers. Still, the subtle humor abounds here if you keep your eyes open. LexCorp references appear along with little touches that can bring a smile (12th ranked Kansas Jayhawks football??).

The acting is superb throughout. Henry Cavill was the runner-up to Daniel Craig for the James Bond role, but he immediately stakes his claim to the Man of Steel. His overall look and amazing physique leave little doubt that he is Superman, and as a bonus, he is plenty of reason for the ladies to purchase a ticket. Hans Zimmer makes no attempt to one-up John Williams' iconic score from the 1978 film, yet he makes his mark, especially during the action sequences. Be prepared as this one is heavy on the Sci-Fi angle, and there is also an interesting Jesus comparison that can be made (he is 33 years on Earth).

Do the right thing has always been the recurring theme for Superman and this movie version helps us understand where the moral fiber was born ... the hint is in the Royals shirt Clark wears. In addition to a terrific Smallville set, we get Laurence Fishburne as Perry White, a role which will surely be expanded in the sequel. It's very interesting to see the Snyder, Goyer, Nolan vision, and if you are still clinging to 1978, you might ask yourself ... Why so serious?

title: not bad
review:
Looks like we'll need to wait a little longer for another Superman film to match the standards set by Richard Donner's Superman. But this film isn't bad.

It's definitely better than Bryan Singer's Superman. The strengths of this film are what Superman Returns lacked: a great cast, a good script, an interesting story, and a powerful music score.

The cast, particularly Russell Crowe, is what saves this film. All are great for their roles. There is even some chemistry between Henry Cavil and Amy Adams, although they don't spend much time together. Unlike Richard Donner's version, this one is less about Superman and Lois than it is about Superman fulfilling his purpose in life.

It's hard to imagine a Superman film without John Williams' memorable score but Hans Zimmer manages to come up with something unique, just as grand and nearly as hummable. It's a powerful, uplifting score befitting of a Superman movie with some very distinct themes. Though the score isn't quite as complete as that by John Williams-- not many music scores these days are-- it's very adequate.

Of course the special effects are great. But they're nothing we haven't seen before. Some of them seem to have been inspired by the Matrix films. But that's fine. Most big budget films have such high quality special effects than they cannot differentiate from one another simply by special effects alone. They need to have-- do I dare say?-- a good cast, story, script, character development, etc. Fortunately, this film has most of that.

I understand this version is supposed to be a grittier, more down to earth Superman. But ironically, it ends up being less realistic than Richard Donner's Superman. It is a little darker but darker doesn't necessarily mean more realistic. It spends too much time on the negative aspects of growing up and too little on the positive. A kid with all those powers can't be all that bad, can it?

Also, this film has more of a science fiction feel which takes us even farther away from reality. It presents us with too many alien ideas, strange technology and technical details that we have a harder time to believe the setting is actually present day on earth. All these alien ideas and details should've been kept in abstract terms as they were in Donner's Superman.

I would've liked to see more interaction between Superman and Lois Lane. And I would've liked for General Zod to appear in later films, not at the beginning, as was done in Donner's version. With General Zod, a man with the same powers as Superman, already appearing in this film, it's hard to imagine there could be a stronger, better foe for Superman without getting weird. There's talk about other aliens like Braniac appearing in the sequel but I'd hate to see the series go off into the deep end into science fiction fantasy.

Basically, Sneider's Superman is a combination of Donner's Superman 1 and 2. Donner's Superman was lightening in a bottle. It appears there will never be a Superman film as good. Special effects do get better in these remakes. Can you imagine Donner's Superman 2 with today's special effects? I'd love to see that.

All in all, Sneider's Superman is a good remake. It has a strong cast, good script and catchy original music score. It has most of the elements that made Donner's Superman great.

review:

title: Superman Returns......Again!!
review: The fan-boys will be out in full force on this one. Although I think the big weekends of cash this flick will do will drown out their cries. I'm just going to give my likes and dislikes. What I liked: (1) Henry Cavill--Did a fine job as Clark/Kal El. Christopher Reeve set the bar at a Air Jordan Level. Brandon Routh really never stood a chance( even though that film didn't give him much to work with. title: From an unbiased perspective.
review:
Not being a fan of Superman and holding little to no knowledge of the background to the character, I think I can give a valid review of Man of Steel.

We begin in the fiery and somewhat complex alien world of Krypton, which could have over faced a few filthy casuals. The visuals and 3d cgi design was on a heavy level of detail on a large scale but for me lacked a beauty and power which carried throughout. There was a deep and repetitive Hanz Zimmer bass which came out every other second (even in the quiet, intense moments), which attempted to bring a sense of power. I think it was brinking obnoxious the amount of times it was used; and it lost effect. The countless explosions were twinned with this especially during a 30 minute destruction scene; exhausting. The score asides this wasn't particularly inspiring or symbolic, but of course gave some energy to the film. On to the casting: Diane Lane, good loving mother, Russell Crowe, top distanced but concerned father figure. The others' acting was pretty average where no performance stood out. I think Amy Adams should stick to rom-coms and kids films, she was too calm and collected for a woman being watched by the world. So overall that was average.

The Cal character was developed with the audience way too loosely. There was one beautiful scene where he is a child and is comforted by his mother. In this we see the emotions of a scared little boy in such a powerful being, part of what makes him as an adult. There are a few almost flashback scenes which are trippy and random so I would have preferred a fluent young man story so we, as an audience, actually feel and side with Clark. I felt this flaw made the film lack emotion and power because of the lack of connection with the audience. Finally, too much blue, needs more red. 7.5/10

DIJ

title: A fairly excellent summer blockbuster.
review: Man of Steel. Without any spoilers, this is how it was for me: The non-linear storytelling is a nice format; though it's not particularly well done, it serves the purpose. The visual effects and overall CG are the best I have ever seen in any motion picture or video. Any motion picture so far, hands down. All the fights and flying scenes are hyper-real, and whenever lasers were involved, I found myself audibly gasping. However, after a little while, it tends to get a wee bit tedious. The relationships in the movie are not particularly well developed, and some people are stupid/helpless enough at times that you want to scream at them. -_- Especially unconvincing is the "bond" between Superman/Lois. Though there are no plot-holes per se, the story is fairly predictable, but then it is Superman after all. :) The dialogues serve their purpose but are OK at best. The score by Zimmer is excellent, though nothing new for him. My only main complaint was that this movie, in a way, compromised Superman's ideology of maintaining peace and order while stopping his villains; not once in any previous movie or graphic novel has he deliberately or otherwise caused this large a scale of random destruction. Sure, his enemies were overpowered and what not, but he should have been shown to try and be more cautious is all. Overall, quite a visual treat; some scenes could have been cut, but it's well worth the money either way.

title: General Zod
review: Man of Steel is one of the first movie to really display the Kryptonians extraordinary power on Earth. No one could have done a better job with this. The story line, though compiled and meddled with, is well presented. The sequence in which Clark learns the full potential of his abilities is pleasant to see. The best work of this movie, however, is General Zod. The character of Zod is impeccable. The way he analyzes his temporary weakness on Earth to master in order to carry his mission is simply beautiful. After watching Man of Steel, I am now a big fan of General Zod. My admiration for Zack Snyder's work on this movie leads to the following questions: Why did Zod have to die? The definition of death on Earth do not apply to Kryptonians. How is it General Zod died, Even with a broken neck (humans perceptions)? Superman could have beating the General in another manner. So that we could have a return of General Zod later on. Also, it would have been nice to have shown either that Clark had learned how to fight or the codex had encoded/embedded some mad fighting skills within his cells. The only way to overcome General Zod, the smart of all his people, including his father's, the sensibility, and the fighting skills needed for their survival. Regardless of all that, General Zod cannot die on Earth. The capital flaw with Man of Steel.

title: Spectacular
review:
MOS might seem loud to some, but I thought it had the perfect balance of character and action. The film seemed to have the whole Superman is Jesus metaphor, but I didn't mind it all. In fact it makes complete sense given the context of the film.

Henry Cavill is very good as Superman. There were a few parts where I could hear his British accent slipping, but otherwise he fit the part, he was very suave and handsome (I'm not gay BTW).

Amy Adams is given a lot to do as Lois Lane. In fact she has a lot more screen time than I expected. The relationship between Superman and Lois is not exactly "great" in this film per say, but Adams and Cavill have very good chemistry between each other, and the fact that Lois knows who Superman is off the bat, made it all the more better.

Michael Shannon is decent as Zod, but I must admit his voice is somewhat of a turn off for me, so I couldn't take him completely serious in the role. The fact that Zod isn't exactly a villain, but someone who believes what he's doing is right, made the portrayal of the character, better than how he was portrayed in Superman 2.

Crowe as Jor-EL is good, but he seemed to be slumming it a little. He seemed to have too little energy.

Fishburne as Perry White was fine, but he really wasn't given enough to do (which is to be expected). He was very demanding and bossy, much like Perry White would be.

Costner and Lane are good, but they didn't have much screen time, so I didn't feel they brought much to the table.

Again the 3D brought nothing new to the table. It was a complete waste of money (as usual).

Also Jenny Olsen (or just Jenny) didn't play much of a role in this film (as I expected), but I must admit she was given a good scene.

I hope this film is successful enough to start a DCMU, however given WB's slow track record; it'll be a long time before we see a DC adaption that isn't Superman or even Batman.

9 / 10

title: Building up a majestic car but forgetting the engine
review:
You keep wanting it to get going and the engine sparks up but fails to turn on and this happens time and again and after waiting in traffic with a faulty engine for hours you find yourself disappointed turning around to go home. (people actually left the theater).

It wasn't unbearable, but it was slow with no real story. I can't blame anyone it is just Superman = clark kent, his parents, his alien race, Louis lane, daily planet, 'saving' earth to become a 'hero' - how many times can you tell this story? I keep waiting for the day the superman story can be as dynamic as batman or even spider man. He does have the best powers but unfortunately he is a boring dude.

Standard big budget 3d effects but loads of unnecessary destruction with a non cohesive story; some people laughed at the cheesy moments but others were too bored to even do that.

title: Finally, a Superman who can throw a punch without sleazy winks
review: I was expecting many things in this movie, crying my eyes out was not one of them. But the way my eyes welled up during the very first sequence in Krypton made me know I was in for something special. This is an origin movie. As any other Superhero origin movie, it has a complex and difficult task. It needs to introduce many characters, build depth, while entertaining the audience. The entertainment part in a Superhero origin movie usually happens after the character's powers are developed. However, in Man of Steel, through impeccable casting, particularly in the form of Russel Crowe who absolutely killed it as Jor-El, and Lane/Costiner, the first half of the movie had its fair share of entertainment while building depth and back story never before seen in a Superman movie. The Krypton scenes are a sight to behold, as the planet is brought into life in a way never before seen on any production. Flashback's of Clark in Smallville carry a lot of emotional depth, building up for the spectacle of action that is the second half of the movie. Seeing the trailer, I was worried the movie would not be able to do the story justice. I felt it wanted to do more than what time would allow, but remarkably, they pulled it off. As seen with the Dark Knight Trilogy, now that the characters have been introduced, the sequel can only be better than what was already a pitch perfect Superman origin movie. I left the movie 100% satisfied with the action a Superman movie deserves, with sore eyes that shed tears I never saw coming. 10/10, with thanks and compliments to the producer, director, writer, and spectacular cast.

title: Could of been so much better
review:
This movie is not great. The movie lacks substance.

It almost feels like the beginning is so drawn out so much that the actual development and transition of Clark into Superman gets rushed. The flash backs into Clarks childhood are interesting, and probably the best parts of the movie. But Once Clark discovers the Kryptonian ship the actual transformation into superman happens in a blink of an eye. I guess he just needed to find his cape and his life finally made sense.

There's little development between Lois and Clark, and yea this will happen in the next film, but there should have been more between these two. The whole movie seems rushed to get to the end, an over done CGI fest that just drags on to the point of ridiculous. Just because he is the man of steel doesn't mean the fight scene needs to feel like an hour.

This movie is just a CGI sell out, it looks amazing, yes, but so what? You can say it should be expected with Zack Snyder directing, well then this guy was not the man for the job.

With the legacy of Superman, this film deserved better.

title: 8/10 Epic beyond proportions, but what else?
review: where to start? I was lucky enough to experience Man of Steel yesterday at a special screening at LaFilmFest. And even though (or maybe because of) my expectations were beyond high, I was mildly disappointed. The entire movie had great CGI and eye candy, and the action was very consistent. The grand scale of the entire movie blew me away, along with the sharp score by Hans Zimmer and the sound mixing. But at times, the dialogue would completely lack subtlety and be predictable. Yes, there were good moralistic and utilitarian themes expressed near the beginning, but it lost it's traction and broke into a full blown action movie with no theme whatsoever. Now most of the actors, notably Henry Cavill's portrayal on the iconic hero, did a decent job, and yet no actor in the amazing cast truly expressed their characters. Many clichés were played across the action, such as the last-minute savior and the revealing of the villain's true form. Despite of Nolan and David Goyer writing the story and script, it lacked many fundamental elements in other Nolan movies. Which brings me to another point. I'd say Zack Snyder is a visual genius, but throughout this movie, all we see in constant racketeering of humanoid shapes and explosions that thicken your ears. The technique is obvious, but lacked much depth. Hans Zimmer's energetic score kept the movie going. The supporting characters are just god-awful. They are flat and do not develop in any way throughout the movie, nor do they have background stories or distinct personalities. Despite of all this, Man of Steel still holds up as a good movie, with thought and a drive to push forward

title: Horrible special effects ruined it
review: Before general zod, movie was 6. After general zod, 0. Holy crap did the special effects guys go over the top bad making this movie.

title: Brilliant Reboot
review:
Man of Steel is an amazing reboot of the Superman Universe. Henry Cavill has captured the essence of Superman more than anyone has since Christopher Reeve. Where Superman Returns, Lois and Clark, and Smallville failed, Man of Steel has prevailed. Cavill is the quintessential Superman, bringing a believable superhero to life. The story, using many modern day movie effects introduces us to a new introduction to the the life and times of Kal El, aka. Superman.

The film is brilliant in the way it uses dream sequences to show the Earth history of Superman. title: The lovechild of the Avengers and the Dark Knight
review:
Now that Marvel superhero films are stealing the limelight at the Box Office and the only (successful) franchise left in the DC stable was Batman, there was a lot of pressure on to 'reboot' Superman (or reboot the 2006 reboot which didn't really hit the mark with fans).

So, seeing as 'The Dark Knight' was a more serious and darker take on the Batman legend, they decided to go the same route with Superman and give him the 'Dark Knight' makeover.

And, it has worked to a degree. Henry Cavill was definitely the right choice to play the 'Man of Steel' and totally nails it in the role. All the other cast members are good, too, but it's Henry who carries the film. Yes, Man of Steel is darker than the average Marvel superhero film, yet not as dark as the Christopher Nolan Batman trilogy. Plus, because Superman's story/powers are more 'fantastical' than Batman's, it has an 'Avengers feel' to some of the (many) action sequences.

As a modern and darker reboot of the Superman legend, it definitely works and fans of the comic shouldn't be too disappointed with the direction it's heading. A lot of people weren't happy with the choice in director (Zack Snyder – 300, Watchmen, Dawn of the Dead 2004), but he seemed to handle the big budget and the various – expected – action scenes. My only gripe was that a lot of the action felt quite computer generated. It would have been nice if it looked as gritty and real as the rest of the film was trying to be. But, overall, I'm looking forward to seeing how the franchise continues.

title: Who allowed this movie to exist?
review:
First off, I gave this movie 2 stars instead of 1 because it is visually impressive. Aside from that, this movie was total garbage.

A lot of the people who argue that this movie is good and that critics always rag on super hero movies due to lack of any artistic or emotional value. I understand this, and I agree that for most super hero movies, it is about being entertaining rather than having great acting and fantastic plots. There are plenty of movies that aren't necessarily "good" in the traditional sense but that I still enjoy because they are fun to watch, like the Fast and Furious series or Expendables, or pretty much any other recent super hero movie. This one managed to be so horrifyingly awful that, despite a few cool fight scenes, it is virtually unwatchable.

The first hour and a half of the movie is pretty much just jumping around between different places and times in Superman's life. This is obviously not uncommon in movies, but in Man of Steel it just feels drawn out and boring. You see him get teased and taunted, which makes you want to see him get some amount of revenge, but there was really only one scene where he lets himself get even, which left me feeling very unsatisfied. He is basically being held back by his father, who is supposed to be his sort of guide into becoming a hero. His dad is so strict on his rule of "don't show off you're super powers", that he doesn't let Superman save his life in front of the towns people, although I feel as though the people would have found it odd that this super buff young guy didn't try to save his father, super powers or not.

This scene is obviously supposed to tug at your heart strings, which it doesn't, at all. I felt no emotional attachment to anyone in this movie, probably due to the barrage of shallow flash backs. They got in a fight right before this scene, kind of like in the Tobey Maguire Spiderman with the fight with Uncle Ben, except in this movie, it is impossible to care at all about it.

Speaking of shallowness and lack of emotion, how about that forced love between Superman and Lois Lane? They probably spent like, collectively a couple of hours alone together and are now madly in love. And how about the worst attempt at humor in the history of the universe? They kiss and she says "They say it all goes down hill after the first kiss" and he says something about that only applying to humans. How is their relationship going to go downhill? They are in the middle of a destroyed New York City, where god knows how many people have just died, which also makes their kiss and light heartedness pretty inappropriate. (By the way, Amy Adams is almost ten years older than Henry Cavill, I think Superman can do better).

Did anyone else notice the super shameless advertising? I don't really care if everyone is driving a BMW or using a Mac, but they fought in front of a Sears, which is pretty thoroughly wrecked aside from the huge intact Sears sign that is constantly in the background.

I have read other reviews about the plot holes, so I won't even go there, but yeah, there is about a million.

In short: Movies can have no substance but still be fun and worth seeing. This is not one of those movies.
